title: Macular Corneal Dystrophy: A Deep Dive into MCD
summary: Macular Corneal Dystrophy (MCD) is a rare, autosomal recessive stromal dystrophy characterized by diffuse corneal haze and ill-defined gray-white opacities. Unlike other stromal dystrophies, it involves the entire corneal thickness and extends to the limbus, significantly impacting vision early in life.

sections.title: Definition & Genetic Basis
content: MCD is a localized manifestation of a systemic error in keratin sulfate metabolism.
Inheritance: Autosomal Recessive (AR) - The 'Odd One Out' among classic stromal dystrophies.
Gene Mutation: CHST6 (Carbohydrate Sulfotransferase 6) located on Chromosome 16q22.
Pathogenesis: Deficiency of corneal sulfotransferase enzyme results in non-sulfated Keratan Sulfate (KS) accumulation.

branches: Severe decrease in Visual Acuity by 2nd-3rd decade
Recurrent corneal erosions (less common than Lattice)
Diffuse stromal haze extending to the LIMBUS

content.mnemonic: Marilyn Monroe Always Gets Her Men
content.explanation: MCD = Alcian Blue (GAGs); Granular = Masson Trichrome (Hyaline); Lattice = Congo Red (Amyloid).

sections.title: Ocular Examination Findings
content: Slit-lamp: Superficial/Deep stromal opacities.
Ground-glass appearance of intervening stroma.
Descemet's Membrane: Guttata-like changes can be seen.
Endothelium: GAG deposits can be found even in the endothelium.
Pachymetry: Shows marked thinning early in the disease.

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup
content: 1. Clinical Slit-lamp Bio-microscopy
2. Anterior Segment OCT: Hyper-reflective deposits + thinning.
3. Confocal Microscopy: Deposits in keratocytes and extracellular matrix.
4. ELISA: For serum Keratan Sulfate (KS) levels (Type determination).
5. Genetic Testing: CHST6 mutation analysis.

sections.title: Management & Treatment Protocol
content: Step 1: Lubrication and Bandage Contact Lenses (BCL) for erosions.
Step 2: Phototherapeutic Keratectomy (PTK) - Only for very superficial deposits.
Step 3: Deep Anterior Lamellar Keratoplasty (DALK) - If endothelium is spared.
Step 4: Penetrating Keratoplasty (PKP) - Gold standard for full-thickness involvement.
Step 5: Post-operative Monitoring - Recurrence is possible in the graft (from host keratocytes).

sections.title: Surgical Nuances
content: DALK is preferred to avoid rejection, but dissection is difficult due to stromal haze.
PKP has high success rates but carries long-term risk of graft failure/rejection.
Recurrence in MCD is generally slower than in Granular or Lattice dystrophies.
Deposits recur from host keratocytes migrating into the donor tissue.

sections.title: Red Flags & Clinical Warnings
content: MCD has the worst visual prognosis among the classic trio.
Corneal thinning: Be cautious of perforation risk during PKP/DALK.
Systemic symptoms? Unlike Mucopolysaccharidosis, MCD is limited to the eye.
Secondary Glaucoma: Possible post-PKP.

sections.title: Landmark Studies & Recent Advances
content: IC3D Classification (2015): Updated MCD to a Category 1 dystrophy (gene known, well-defined).
Gene Therapy: Research into AAV-mediated CHST6 replacement is ongoing in animal models.
Enzyme Replacement: Investigations into topical sulfotransferase mimics.
Large-scale cohort studies in South India (Tamil Nadu) show high prevalence due to consanguinity.

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: If you see a haze that reaches the LIMBUS, think Macular Corneal Dystrophy.
If the cornea is THIN, think Macular. If it's normal/thick, think Granular.
MCD is the only AR stromal dystrophy; the rest are usually AD.
MCD deposits are Alcyan Blue positive (G-A-G: Macular, Alcian, GAGs).
